newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan mulls tightening China investments - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan mulls tightening China investments - paper.

text.p: Taiwan would adopt a more cautious policy on the island's investments in rival China in 1997, the mass circulation United Daily News reported on Wednesday.

The paper quoted Economics Minister Wang Chih-kang as saying that the government planned to set up "reasonable" limits to regulate Taiwanese investments on the mainland, especially those by its powerful conglomerates. It did not elaborate.
About 25,000 Taiwan firms have poured more than US$20 billion into mainland China since a political thaw in the late 1980s, but the flow eased in 1996.

Frustrated by a political impasse with China and a sagging domestic economy, the government has openly expressed its concern that Taiwan risked becoming too dependent on the economy of its arch rival -- and thus politically vulnerable.
Wang was quoted as saying that his ministry would invent a warning system to avoid risky dependence on the mainland and might tighten its reviews on projects in China.
Beijing has considered the island a rebel-held province since the Nationalists fled to Taiwan at the end of the 1949 Chinese civil war.
